ordered_diagnoses: Melanoma metastatic to the liver with unknown primary
Malignant melanoma of unknown primary origin with hepatic metastasis

s1.syndrome_frame: Incidental hepatic tumors with abnormal liver function tests and characteristic radiologic and histopathologic features
salient_findings: Multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
Uneven arterial enhancement and washout in the portal venous and delayed phases on CT
Epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments on biopsy
key_facts: Hepatic tumors found incidentally during routine check-up
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
No medical history of liver disease
Smokes 2-5 cigarettes daily for ten years
Abdomen soft and non-tender without ascites
Tumor markers (AFP, CEA, CA19-9, CA125) within normal limits
Immunohistochemical staining positive for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
